system_description.narrative_title: Multipolar volatility: energy shocks, war fronts and tech rivalry
system_description.narrative_summary: The international system is an open, stressed network where concurrent high-intensity conflicts (Middle East and Russia–Ukraine), strategic competition between major powers (US–China–Russia), and acute energy-market strains interact and amplify one another. Supply-chain and technology frictions—especially over chips, AI and satellite services—are now geopolitical levers alongside sanctions, proxy attacks and unilateral asset moves, producing fragmentation of alliances and rising systemic fragility.
system_description.scope: State actors (US, China, Russia, Iran, Saudi, EU members, Ukraine, Israel, North Korea, others), non-state combatants (Houthis, proxy networks), global energy and shipping systems (oil, diesel, refinery and tanker flows), high‑tech ecosystems (semiconductors, AI export controls, satellite comms), financial sanctions/asset flows, and critical infrastructure vulnerabilities.
system_description.super_system: The global political‑economic‑security order (the international system of states, markets, transnational firms and institutions)

variables.name: Gulf maritime and regional escalation
variables.description: Iran-backed Houthi forces, Iran, Saudi Arabia and other Gulf states are engaged in a widening campaign of maritime and infrastructure strikes that is shifting regional security dynamics and days-to-days risk to shipping and coastal assets.

variables.name: High-intensity Russia–Ukraine war
variables.description: Russia and Ukraine remain locked in an intensified, evolving military campaign marked by cross-border strikes, expanded drone operations and territorial offensives that are reshaping battlefield control and wartime tactics.

variables.name: Global energy market squeeze
variables.description: Major producers, oil traders and international agencies are reacting to concurrent supply disruptions and strategic stock releases—creating a persistent diesel and fuel-market squeeze that is shifting price formation and policy interventions worldwide.

variables.name: US–China technology and trade competition
variables.description: The United States and China are escalating competition over semiconductors, AI and export controls while partners in Europe and Asia recalibrate access and industrial policy, shifting global tech supply chains and governance norms.

variables.name: Western alliance strain and policy unpredictability
variables.description: Political shifts in the United States and policy divergences among European partners are producing strains in intelligence-sharing, military support and coordinated sanctions, altering the cohesion and decision-making of Western alliances.
